1. IS kinds MECE OVER unmatched_reasons' GAP REASONS. unmatched_reasons (infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/_scope/resolve.py:555-593 @b3a148044f, unedited by this order) emits EXACTLY three reason codes via a closed if/elif/else with no other branch: CROSS-FIRM (:582-584), UNPROJECTED-ID (:585-588), NOT-IN-DIRECTORY (:589-591) -- the function's own docstring (:561-569) enumerates the same three, so the SUBTRACTION (3 documented minus 3 coded = 0 uncovered) holds over the function's OWN declared domain. enforce.py's kinds histogram (Enforcer.resolve_now, 'gap_kinds = _histogram(g["reason"].split(":")[0] for g in gaps)' @b3a148044f) buckets EVERY gap unmatched_reasons returns for the granted set, one bucket per gap by construction (each gap carries exactly one reason string), so kinds is MECE over unmatched_reasons' domain BY CONSTRUCTION -- it cannot emit a key the function does not produce, and it cannot drop a gap the function does produce. THE CAVEAT, stated because the domain choice is itself a claim (CLAUDE.md Rule 24): kinds is MECE only over the SERVED case's population -- an id that never reaches advisor_grant at all (no advisors[advisor_id] entry, ownership schema_version mismatch, or the whole permitted set ending up empty) never generates a gap and never reaches the disclosure field, because a REFUSAL carries no data and no unprojected_grant. So the taxonomy is complete for 'why did a granted-and-directory-checked id not make it into a SERVED response', and says nothing about, and does not claim to say anything about, why a request was refused outright.

2. DOES THE SEAM'S VINTAGE TRAVEL WITH THE SERVED RESPONSE. NO, measured by reading every field the disclosure carries: unprojected_grant is exactly {count, denominator, kinds} (infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/_authz/served.py response_envelope() @b3a148044f) -- no vintage, no seam identifier, no as_of date. The SERVED path's response_envelope() call (Entry.handle, served.py @b3a148044f) does not pass business_date at all (unlike the REFUSAL path's refuse(...) call, which does via artifact_business_date(ctx)) -- so a served response's outer envelope carries no seam or directory vintage either, only whatever the route's own data payload happens to include. Consequence: if the 49financial identity-bridge seam (custodian_key_seam.json, dated 2026-09-16, row IRPT_BCKEND-W1-S25) is re-cut with a newer snapshot, an advisor's served k and unprojected_grant.count can both change between two calls, and NOTHING in the response lets a caller or a later reader distinguish 'the same partial, re-observed' from 'a different partial, because the seam moved'. This bears directly on the consumer obligation's own bar ('was the partial ever actually shown, an artifact not a recollection') -- the artifact as currently shipped answers WHAT was shown but not AS OF WHAT DATA.

3. IS FWD-1/2/5's SERVED PATH NOW REACHABLE FOR A REAL ADVISOR. At the UNIT level, yes for the shape of grant row W1-S27 named: this cell's OWN fixture (OWNERSHIP_PARTIAL_UNPROJECTED, 3 granted/1 unprojected/2 permitted) is SERVED end to end through the real Enforcer (battery arm a, this run). At the DEPLOYED level, YES, measured this pass (second pass, arm (e)): the live request against the deployed bytes through the REAL served.Entry.enforcer_for now SERVES abby_horton/49financial with k=21 permitted and unprojected_grant={count:12,denominator:33} disclosed (the live ownership map's account count moved from 43 to 33 between the two cells' measurement windows via a concurrent unrelated refresh, row W1-S30; the served/refused SHAPE is unchanged). Per firm: inflection's live ownership map is ABSENT (loaders.load_ownership's own rule: an absent map reads as {schema_version:1, advisors:{}}) and cottonwood's is PRESENT but EMPTY (0 advisors) -- so for BOTH of those firms a real FIRM_ADVISOR request today hits the empty-permitted-set branch VACUOUSLY (0 of 0 grants) and is refused EMPTY_GRANT regardless of this order's inversion, because there is no live grant population to serve a partial FROM.

4. WHAT IRPT_FNTEND MUST RENDER. Per the consumer-obligation row (IRPT_BCKEND-W1-S28, this order's own arm (c)) and the ruling's own words: a VISIBLE partial indicator whenever unprojected_grant.count > 0, so the answer to 'was the partial ever actually shown' is an artifact and not a recollection. The three fields available to render from are count, denominator and kinds -- e.g. a 'showing K of D accounts' indicator sourced from count/denominator, with kinds available for a more detailed 'N unresolved, M cross-firm, ...' breakdown if IRPT_FNTEND chooses one. This cell does not prescribe the component; it ships the field and the obligation, and closes the obligation only when IRPT_FNTEND's own L4 carrier states what it built against it (per the row's disarm_owner, 1.0.0_SA_CTO).
